market_holds: Spot $0.7411 at 18:09 UTC on 2026-11-19 (sealed baseline). That is -42% over 20 sessions, -8.8% over 5, -87% from the 52-week high, 2% above the 52-week low, and down about 61% from the $1.91 close before the Q2 print (Yahoo daily bars). It fell 17.5% on 2026-11-04 on 1.0m shares with no company filing I could find. No usable option chain, so there is no implied move. Realised vol is 87% annualised, which gives a 5.5% one-day deadband. Earnings reactions at the open: Q1 (2026-05-14, guide cut plus a 25% layoff) -31%, from $4.14 to a $2.845 open; Q2 (2026-08-13, guide reaffirmed, FCF $9.6m) +13%, from $1.91 to a $2.16 open. Consensus for Q3 is about $41.5m revenue and $0.05 adjusted EPS (Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-11 via Finviz), against $39.0m revenue and $13.0m adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2025. Sell-side price targets of $3-5 are stale against a $0.74 price. The FY26 guide is $165-170m revenue and $45-50m adjusted EBITDA, reaffirmed 2026-08-13. That needs H2 revenue of $86.8-91.8m (H2 2025: about $85.3m) and H2 EBITDA of $28.3-33.3m (H2 2025: about $28.5m), after H1 EBITDA fell 44% to $16.7m. The CFO said seasonality is strongest in Q4, so Q3 alone does not settle the guide. Balance sheet: borrowings $122.3m against $8.8m cash and $33.3m of liquidity, and $26.5m of OddsJam deferred consideration now current (due 2027-04-01, up to 70% payable in unregistered shares). The 6-K liquidity table puts $120.5m of borrowings and interest due in one to two years. Market cap is about $26m on about 35.5m shares. Short interest was about 0.97m shares (about 2.7%, 5.2 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement. The equity is priced as distressed: about 3.5x EV to guided EBITDA counting the earnout, so a guide cut and dilution are largely priced. The line it trades on is whether the FY guide holds, plus how the earnout is settled and the facility refinanced.
view: This is a distressed, thinly traded affiliate and sports-data name, and the print turns on two things: whether the FY26 EBITDA guide holds, and what management says about the $26.5m earnout and the facility maturing in 2027-28. Q3 should mechanically show sequential EBITDA recovery from $7.7m. The $6.5m of H2 cost savings is about $3.25m a quarter, and data grows in the teens, so Q3 EBITDA around $11-14m is plausible. A Q4-weighted guide can be held or narrowed to the low end at Q3, and the CFO said in August that they had 'reset'. The peer reads since the last call disagree with each other. Catena Media pre-warned on 2026-10-16 and reported North America -29% in Q3, citing zero-click search, ranking pressure and cautious, consolidating operator budgets. Better Collective (2026-11-19) grew North America 28% on prediction-market spend, but sports margins went against it (-EUR6.5m) and the shares fell 8.5%. DraftKings' and FanDuel's US marketing spend rose sharply in Q3, which helps non-SEO affiliate demand. Google SERPs in iGaming were volatile again in September, after the March and May updates hurt affiliates. Grandstand sits between those two peers: about two-thirds of its marketing is non-SEO, but SEO still fell 10% in Q2. At $26m of market cap the equity is already priced for a guide cut plus heavy share-settled dilution. A reaffirm, or a cash plan for the earnout, could squeeze it 20-40%. A guide cut with share settlement, a refinancing warning or going-concern language could take it down another 15-30%. I cannot tell from public evidence which branch comes, so I hold no directional view. I put p_up just above 50 because so much bad news is already in the price, and the Q3 numbers themselves should look sequentially better.

recommendation.reason: The direction depends on whether management holds the FY26 guide and how it settles the earnout and refinances. Neither has left a public trace since the 2026-08-13 call. The peer evidence is split: Catena's North America fell 29% while Better Collective's rose 28% and US operators' marketing spend surged. The roughly 61% fall since Q2 already prices a cut and dilution, so a long-the-squeeze or short-the-cut view has no dated mechanism behind it.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Two outcomes would decide it. A plan to pay the April 2027 earnout in cash, or an announced refinancing, together with an EBITDA guide reaffirmed at $45m or better, would make it a likely large up-move. An EBITDA guide cut below about $42m together with share settlement of the earnout would make it a likely down-move.

self_critique: The strongest case for a direction is up. At a $26m market cap with about $45m of guided EBITDA, even a modest trim plus sequential Q3 recovery could set off a violent relief rally, as Q2's +13% did from a less distressed level. The tax-loss and sub-$1 selling that drove the November slide is mechanical, not informational. The strongest case for down: managements in this sector cut at Q3 (Gambling.com itself did in Q3 2025), Catena shows the SEO and operator-budget damage was industry-wide in Q3, and the steady 42% slide may be informed selling ahead of a share-settled earnout or a refinancing warning.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced in') helped: the balance-sheet arithmetic shows distress pricing, not awareness alone. P3's 'freshest data first' found useful peer prints, but they conflicted. Company-specific alternative data (traffic, app ranks) was not reachable in time, and the last call left nothing quantified for Q3.
